title: Far-pair offset collimation with separate budgets

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s modulo N, the far-pair designated-offset algorithm in proof.md, with n=ceil(log2 N), its public integer schedule and two deterministic budgets, and its finite-length fallback, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 from independent ideal copies. The same configuration jointly has branchwise charged sequential work O(2^((9/8) sqrt(n log2 n) + sqrt(n))), with exact growth index 1/2.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s modulo N, the far-pair designated-offset algorithm in proof.md, with n=ceil(log2 N), its public integer schedule and two deterministic budgets, and its finite-length fallback, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 from independent ideal copies. The same configuration jointly has peak allocated classical space O(n^2) bits on every branch, with exact growth index 0.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s modulo N, the far-pair designated-offset algorithm in proof.md, with n=ceil(log2 N), its public integer schedule and two deterministic budgets, and its finite-length fallback, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 from independent ideal copies. The same configuration jointly has peak allocated quantum space O(n) qubits on every branch, with exact growth index 0.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s modulo N, the far-pair designated-offset algorithm in proof.md, with n=ceil(log2 N), its public integer schedule and two deterministic budgets, and its finite-length fallback, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 from independent ideal copies. The same configuration jointly has total acquired copies O(2^((1/4) sqrt(n log2 n) - (1/4) sqrt(n))) on every branch, including all failed attempts and discards, with exact growth index 1/2.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s modulo N, the far-pair designated-offset algorithm in proof.md, with n=ceil(log2 N), its public integer schedule and two deterministic budgets, and its finite-length fallback, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 from independent ideal copies. The same configuration jointly has guaranteed malformed fraction epsilon(n)=0, requiring independent ideal copies.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
